intro_md: 🎧 **12 min. A listening lesson about sounds.** Why you can't hear small words – learn the squeezed sounds, then **hear them in a real conversation** straight away.

parts.title: Small words get squeezed
parts.md:
In natural speech, small words lose sounds and **join the word before**. You know these words when you **read** them – but in speech they are only **one short sound**:

| You read | You hear | Sounds like |
|---|---|---|
| you will | **you'll** | /juːl/ – one syllable |
| I have | **I've** | /aɪv/ |
| it is / it has | **it's** | /ɪts/ – same sound for both! |
| I would / I had | **I'd** | /aɪd/ – same sound for both! |
| he is / he has | **he's** | /hiːz/ |
| we have | **we've** | /wiːv/ |

💡 **How to know which one?** Look at the next word:
- *it's **been*** → it **has** (been = has been) · *it's **long*** → it **is**
- *I'd **love*** → I **would** · *I'd **better*** → I **had**

👂 **Listen:** each sentence twice – first **full** (slow, every word), then **natural** (squeezed). Then the last two sentences are only natural. **Tap any line** to hear it again. Try to **whisper along** with the natural version.

listen.text: You will get used to it.
You'll get used to it.
I have lived here ten years.
I've lived here ten years.
It is a long day.
It's a long day.
It has been a long day.
It's been a long day.
He is starting today.
He's starting today.
I would love another coffee.
I'd love another coffee.
I had better go home.
I'd better go home.
She's been here two days, and she's already got lost twice.
You'll be fine. It's normal. We've all been there.

parts.title: Real talk: Nam and Jess after work
parts.md:
Now the same small sounds in a **real conversation** at normal speed – Nam stops at Jess's café after his first day.

Train your ears – the words are hidden at first:
1. 👂 **Listen without the words** – twice. Count the squeezed sounds you catch: *it's · I'd · you'll · I've · he's · we've*.
2. 📄 **Show transcript** – listen + read. **Tap any line** you missed to hear just that part again.
3. 👂 **Hide it** and listen one last time – the squeezed words should now jump out.

listen.text: Hey, Nam! You look tired. How's it going?
So far so good, but it's been a long day. I've met about ten people.
Ten! I'd forget all their names.
I already have. Well, most of them. I'd better write them down tonight.
Don't worry. You'll learn them in a week. It's always like that.
I hope so. Tom's really nice, but he talks so fast. I'd love him to slow down a bit.
Ha! He's from Manchester. That's just how he talks. You'll get used to it.
I'm sure I will. Anyway, I'd love a coffee. What's good today?
The flat white. It's been popular all week. Sit down – I'll bring it over.
Thanks, Jess. You've been really kind since I arrived.
That's what neighbours are for. We've all been new somewhere.

parts.title: Quick check + how was it?
parts.md: A few quick questions – tap an answer, you see right away if it's right. Then tell me how much you understood, ask me anything below, and 📤 **Submit**.

questions.q: How much did you understand? Write a number, e.g. 80
